title: Quantized Margin Controller for Dynamic GPU Balancing
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build a controller (Quantized Margin Controller, QMC) that dynamically allocates GPU memory margins across weights, KV cache, and activations. The goal is to minimize tail latency variance and OOM events for mixed workloads by: (1) using light-weight online quantization to reduce KV/activation footprint when pressure is predicted, (2) creating transient 'spill lanes' that opportunistically place cold KV shards into host-pinned memory or NVMe for microbursts, and (3) adjusting continuous-batching window sizes per-model to exploit the new margin without impacting P95 latency targets.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token latency stays within 1.2x of baseline for 95% of traffic after enabling QMC on canary fleet
End-to-end OOMs reduced by >= 75% on canary workloads with mixed sequence lengths
Average cost-per-token (GPU time) does not increase by more than 8% on production mixes
Telemetry: new metrics (qmc_margin_utilization, kv_spill_rate, quantized_activation_ratio) emit and show expected ranges
Automated rollback triggers if OOM or latency regressions exceed thresholds for 10 minutes
implementation_notes: Controller loop runs every 250ms in the serving agent with exponential backoff under stable conditions
Predictive model: lightweight XGBoost trained on slot-level telemetry (recent seq len histogram, active_kv_bytes, weight_residency) to predict 1s memory pressure and recommend margin delta
Online quantization modes: 8-bit per-tensor dynamic quantization for activations; 4-bit asymmetric quant for cold KV shards when read frequency < threshold
Spill lanes abstraction: memory tier API to move KV shards to host-pinned memory (zero-copy read path) then NVMe fallback; maintain versioned pointers in the actor registry
Continuous-batching policy adjustment: target batch window shrinks by factor proportional to predicted margin deficit, but never below 5ms to preserve throughput
Safety: do not quantize model weights; weights residency policy must preserve full-precision residency for pinned replicas
decisions: Use online quantization of activations and KV (not weights) to avoid quality regressions
Prefer host-pinned memory for first-level spill to reduce read latency vs NVMe cold lane
Run controller in serving agent (local) instead of centralized controller to reduce reaction latency and single point of failure
Expose qmc_mode to customers on Dedicated as opt-in; Hosted default = balanced
blockers: Finalize host-pinned memory allocator API (infra ticket ENG-881920 may overlap)
Need updated KV shard descriptor to support soft migration pointers (responsibility: model-onboarding team)
Security review for host-pinned memory access patterns pending (security team)
Benchmark harness for mixed sequence-length workload generation still in progress (ENG-30945)
test_plan: Unit tests for quantization conversion and recovery paths (simulate quant-decode/encode roundtrips)
Integration test: KV spill + host-pinned read path with fault injection (packet loss, read latency spikes)
Perf benchmark: run production-sampled mix for 24h compare OOM rate, P95 latency, and cost-per-token vs baseline
A/B canary: 5% traffic on canary pool for 48h with aggressive mode toggled via remote config
Chaos: induce heavy multi-tenant memory pressure and assert automatic rollbacks do not cause cascading failures
rollout_plan: Developer preview in dev cluster with synthetic mixes (Week 1)
Canary on non-critical fleet (5%) with balanced mode (Week 2)
Expand canary to 20% and enable conservative mode for latency-sensitive models (Week 3)
Gradual ramp to 100% on dedicated pools that opt-in; Hosted default remains off until validation (Week 5)
Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window and automatic cost/quality regression report
